clue.text: Lead story on poor diving result?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a front-page news story given big, bold treatment
second meaning: the spray of water a clumsy dive throws up

explanation.surface: A newspaper headline about a disappointing diving performance.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a sports report on a bad dive; in fact both halves define the same word, joined by 'on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalists use the word for a sensational front-page story, and divers are marked down for the spray a bad entry makes.

clue.text: Poor young son caught in obvious scam, held in compound

indicators.note: something caught in something else sits inside it, so the young son goes between the two words that follow
being held in an enclosure means being surrounded by it, so everything before goes inside the compound

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure for animals
overt means plain to see
Y is a standard abbreviation for young
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
a trick is a con or swindle

explanation.surface: A poor young man is caught up in a blatant con and ends up locked in a compound.
explanation.walkthrough: Two layers of containment: the young son's two letters sit inside the obvious scam, and that whole string is then enclosed in the animal pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone poverty-stricken is extremely poor, so the single adjective is a straight synonym.

clue.text: "German car's crap!" — said loud enough to be heard

parts.note: Audi is a German car maker

indicators.note: said means spoken out, so the words before are to be judged by how they sound rather than how they are spelt

parts.note: bull, short for bullshit, means nonsense or crap; spoken quickly it gives the ending sound

explanation.surface: Someone loudly declares that a German car is rubbish, in a voice everyone can hear.
explanation.walkthrough: AUDI is taken as written; only the second part is a sound-alike, and a loose one: BULL said quickly matches the unstressed -BLE ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Audible describes sound at a volume the ear can pick up, which the definition spells out in plain words.

clue.text: Worker on strike finally submits to police restraint

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
to cuff is to strike with the hand

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the next word, keeping only its closing letter

parts.note: the last letter of submits

explanation.surface: A striking worker eventually gives in to the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On strike' suggests industrial action, but 'on' just places the worker before the word for hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Handcuffs are the linked metal rings police use to restrain a suspect's wrists.

clue.text: Arrived, taking parking place by tent area

indicators.note: taking means absorbing something into itself, so the next words go inside the word for arrived

parts.note: came means arrived
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
to sit something somewhere is to place it there

explanation.surface: Someone turns up and grabs a parking spot beside the tents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parking place' reads as one idea but splits into P and a verb for put.
explanation.definitionFit: A campsite is the ground set aside where people pitch tents.

clue.text: Charlady showing tolerance not to work

indicators.note: to work something is to knead or rework it, so the remaining letters get rearranged
not means leaving out, so the word for permissiveness loses the little word that follows the negation

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, then removed

explanation.surface: A charwoman shows she is patient with not having to go to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not to' tells you to drop the letters TO from TOLERANCE; what remains is the fodder for 'work'. A charlady is a British term for a woman paid to clean houses or offices.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlady, or char, is a woman hired to clean, so she is a cleaner by trade.

clue.text: Farah suit's about design

parts.note: Mo Farah, the British Olympic distance runner

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the word for suit is read in the other direction

parts.note: to suit is to fit, as in that dress fits you

explanation.surface: A comment on the pattern of the athlete Mo Farah's suit.
explanation.walkthrough: Mo Farah is a famous British long-distance runner; his first name is the opening piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A motif is a recurring pattern or design element, as in a fabric or artwork.

clue.text: Jack's best friends?

parts.note: surface reading: the pets a man named Jack loves, since a dog is man's best friend
setter's reading: a jack tar is a sailor, and his closest companions are fellow old sailors

explanation.walkthrough: Jack, or jack tar, is an old name for a sailor; experienced sailors are nicknamed after the 'man's best friend' animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Veteran sailors are known by this nickname, and as a sailor's shipmates they are his closest companions.

clue.text: Unusually, Ian Holm's due late for film

indicators.note: unusually means not in the normal way, so the letters that follow are put in a different order

parts.note: the fodder letters, taken as written

explanation.surface: The actor Ian Holm, unusually, is running late for his film.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian Holm was a real British actor, which makes the surface a plausible film-set story.
explanation.definitionFit: Thelma & Louise is the 1991 Ridley Scott road movie, so it is an example of a film.

clue.text: Key to study in evil gets proof

parts.note: E is a musical key

indicators.note: in places the word for study inside the word for wickedness

parts.note: vice means wickedness
a den is a private study room

explanation.surface: Studying evil is the key to finding proof, like a detective.
explanation.definitionFit: Evidence is what establishes a fact, so it serves as proof in a court or argument.

clue.text: Thai starter with pork quarters is a capital course

indicators.note: a starter comes at the beginning of a meal, so only the opening letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the first letter of Thai
ham is cured pork
east and south, two of the compass quarters

explanation.surface: A restaurant menu: a Thai starter and a pork main make a first-class course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital course' sounds like an excellent dish, but course here is a watercourse running through the capital, London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thames is the river that flows through London, the capital of England.

clue.text: Poet's going round with loose woman

indicators.note: going round means turning to face the other way, so the word for poet is read backwards

parts.note: a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: A poet keeps company with a disreputable woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Drab is an archaic noun for a slattern or prostitute, a crossword-friendly sense alongside the adjective for dull.

clue.text: Potential difficulties with fishing kit?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a situation likely to cause complicated trouble once opened
second meaning, literal: a tin of bait an angler carries

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal reading of a phrase normally used as an idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: Opening a can of worms is an idiom for starting trouble, while literally it is bait for anglers.

clue.text: Half army runs away having lost heart, coming back for me

indicators.note: half keeps just one of the two equal parts of the word that follows

parts.note: the second half of the word army

indicators.note: coming back means returning the other way, so the shortened word is read right to left
losing heart means dropping the central letter of the word for running away

parts.note: flees means runs away

explanation.surface: Half the army deserts, demoralised, and comes back to get me.
explanation.walkthrough: FLEES loses its middle E, and the four letters left are turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Myself is the emphatic form of me, used when the speaker refers to themselves.

clue.text: Plant, say, about 1,000 new carrots

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the thousand
new suggests a fresh version, so the word after it is reshaped into a different order

parts.note: taken as written
K, from kilo, stands for a thousand

explanation.surface: A gardening note: a plant surrounded by a thousand new carrots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like greenery beside the carrots, but it is Robert Plant, Led Zeppelin's singer; 'say' marks him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Plant, lead singer of Led Zeppelin, is a famous example of a rock star.

clue.text: Snip article from new cigar trade magazine

indicators.note: new signals a fresh arrangement, so the remaining letters are reordered
to snip is to cut away, so one letter is cut out of the fodder

parts.note: A is the indefinite article
taken as written

explanation.surface: An editor trims an article for a new tobacco trade magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Magazine' looks like a publication beside 'article', but it is the ammunition holder of a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartridge can be a magazine in the sense of a case of ammunition or a clip loaded into a gun or camera.

clue.text: Level and prepare surroundings for play area

parts.note: a stage is a level or phase reached
to set is to prepare, as in set the table

explanation.surface: Instructions to flatten and get ready the ground around a children's playground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play area' suggests a playground, but the play is a theatrical one.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage set is the scenery that surrounds the acting area during a theatre production.

clue.text: Soldier, with horse that was winning, laughed nervously

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
gee-gee is a childish word for a horse
led means was ahead in a race

explanation.surface: A soldier, backing a horse that was in the lead, laughed nervously.
explanation.definitionFit: To giggle is to laugh in a silly, often nervous way, so the past tense matches.

clue.text: Look! Miliband was a hot topic on Twitter

definitions.text: was a hot topic on Twitter

parts.note: a look in fashion is a trend or style
Ed Miliband, then leader of the Labour Party

explanation.surface: An exclamation that the politician Ed Miliband has gone viral on Twitter.
explanation.walkthrough: Ed Miliband led Britain's Labour Party when the puzzle appeared; 'Look!' is a noun for a style, not a command.
explanation.definitionFit: On social media a subject that trended was among the most discussed, which is what being a hot topic means.

clue.text: Prepared me to come in for a cure

indicators.note: to come in for something is to replace it, so one piece swaps out a letter of another

parts.note: ready means prepared
taken as written
taken as written, the letter that is replaced

explanation.surface: Someone is all set to come in for a treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: The final 'a' is not an article but the letter of READY that ME displaces.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy is a medicine or treatment that cures an illness.

clue.text: Cool men sport an eyeglass!

indicators.note: sport here hints at play or frolic, so the letters before it are tossed into a new order

parts.note: the fodder letters, taken as written

explanation.surface: Fashionable men wear a single lens for show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sport' reads as a verb meaning to wear proudly, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A monocle is a single lens worn in one eye, an old-fashioned eyeglass.

clue.text: Drink for red-headed porter?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a fizzy spiced soft drink
second meaning, whimsical: ginger means red-haired and porter is a dark beer

explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' suggests a hotel employee with red hair, but porter is a type of dark ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger beer is a soft drink, and read literally the words describe a red-haired beer.

clue.text: Automaton runs rings round second-rate model

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the rings enclose the second-class grade

parts.note: two rings, each an O shape
B is the grade below A
the Model T Ford

explanation.surface: An automated machine outperforms an inferior model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs rings round' is an idiom for outclassing, but here each word does a separate job.
explanation.definitionFit: A robot is a machine that performs tasks automatically, which is what an automaton is.

clue.text: Being in A Chorus Line on stage is a gas

parts.note: surface padding: the musical's title around the hidden span

indicators.note: being in means lying within, so the letters sit inside the run of words that follow

parts.note: the end of line and the start of on run together
surface padding completing the theatre picture

explanation.surface: Performing in the musical A Chorus Line on stage is great fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A gas' is slang for something fun, but here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Neon is a noble gas, used in glowing stage and shop signs.

clue.text: TV company's party used to be good place to see stars

definitions.text: used to be good place to see stars

parts.note: Sky is the British satellite TV broadcaster
Lab is the abbreviation for the Labour Party

explanation.surface: A TV company's party was once the place to spot celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars' suggests celebrities at a showbiz party, but it means stars in space.
explanation.definitionFit: Skylab was the American space station of the 1970s, a former vantage point for observing the stars.

clue.text: Finished first scene with leading character as a teacher

parts.note: did means finished, as in did the job
Act I, where a play's first scene falls

indicators.note: leading means at the front, so only the opening letter of the following word is used

parts.note: the first letter of character

explanation.surface: A director finishes the opening scene with the lead actor playing a teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading character' sounds like a play's star, but it is just the first letter of the word character.
explanation.definitionFit: Didactic means intended to instruct, so it describes behaving in the manner of a teacher.

clue.text: Posh new sweetheart's daughter on silly diet, not yet checked

indicators.note: silly means foolish or muddled, so the following word is jumbled

parts.note: U means upper-class
N is an abbreviation for new
read as the heart of sweet: the middle letter of that five-letter word
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter
the letters of diet in a new order

explanation.surface: A posh new girlfriend's daughter is on a faddy diet nobody has checked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetheart' splits into sweet and heart, the heart of sweet being its middle letter. U is an old label for upper-class speech and manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Unedited copy has not yet been revised or checked by an editor.

clue.text: Number for cab? No thanks!

indicators.note: no means without, so the word that follows is taken away from the word for cab

parts.note: a taxi is a cab
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: Someone turning down a taxi: 'Cab? No thanks!'
explanation.walkthrough: Removing TA from TAXI leaves XI, the Roman numeral that is then written out in words; ta is British slang for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleven is a number, here reached through its Roman numeral form.
